title: Bargaining in the bazaar
setting: In Istanbul's Grand Bazaar a blue plate in a small ceramics shop catches your eye. Here, prices are made to be bargained.
goal: Ask a price, bargain it down, and know when to walk away.

cast.name: Dükkân sahibi
cast.why: A shopkeeper you don't know gets *siz*, however friendly he is, and even if he says *sen* to you.

cast.name: Çırak
cast.why: A boy running errands for the shop: *sen*.

nodes.tr: Hoş geldiniz! Buyurun, bakın. Bakmak bedava!
nodes.en: Welcome! Come in, have a look. Looking is free!
nodes.note: *Bakmak bedava*, “looking costs nothing”, is a classic line of the bazaar.

turn.prompt: Ask how much the blue plate is.

replies.tr: Hoş bulduk. Bu mavi tabak ne kadar?
replies.en: Thank you. How much is this blue plate?

replies.tr: Bu mavi tabak ne kadar güzel!
replies.en: How beautiful this blue plate is!
replies.why: A compliment, and he'll love it, but you haven't asked the price yet.
No accusative here: the plate is the subject of the question. *Bu mavi tabak ne kadar?*

nodes.tr: Bu el yapımı. Bin iki yüz lira.

turn.prompt: Say it's very expensive, and ask for a discount.

replies.en: That's very expensive! Will you give me a discount?
accept: Çok pahalı! Biraz indirim yapar mısınız?

replies.en: That's very expensive! Will you give me a discount?
accept: Çok pahalı! Biraz indirim yapar mısın?

replies.why: You can, but in the bazaar the first price is only an opening: everyone bargains.

replies.en: That's very cheap! Will you give me a discount?
replies.why: *Ucuz* means cheap. Too much is *pahalı*: *Çok pahalı!*

react.tr: Ucuz mu? O zaman hemen alın!
react.en: Cheap? Then buy it right away!

nodes.tr: Değil mi? El yapımı! Bin iki yüz lira.

turn.prompt: Say it's very expensive, and ask for a discount.

replies.en: That's very expensive! Will you give me a discount?
accept: Çok pahalı! Biraz indirim yapar mısınız?

replies.en: That's very expensive! Will you give me a discount?
accept: Çok pahalı! Biraz indirim yapar mısın?

replies.why: You can, but in the bazaar the first price is only an opening: everyone bargains.

replies.en: That's very cheap! Will you give me a discount?
replies.why: *Ucuz* means cheap. Too much is *pahalı*: *Çok pahalı!*

react.tr: Ucuz mu? O zaman hemen alın!
react.en: Cheap? Then buy it right away!

nodes.tr: Sizin için bin lira olsun. Son fiyat!
nodes.en: For you, let's say 1,000. That's my final price!
nodes.note: *Son fiyat*, the final price, is rarely final.

turn.prompt: Offer 700 lira, or say you'll look at other shops.

replies.tr: Teşekkürler, ama başka dükkânlara da bakacağım.
replies.en: Thanks, but I'll look at other shops too.
accept: Teşekkürler, ama başka bir dükkâna bakacağım.
Teşekkür ederim, ama başka dükkânlara da bakacağım.

replies.tr: Bin beş yüz lira olur mu?
replies.why: That's more than he's asking! Offer less: *Yedi yüz lira olur mu?*

nodes.note: Shops in the bazaar often send a boy for tea while the bargaining goes on.

nodes.tr: Yedi yüz mü? Çok az! Sekiz yüz elli olsun.
nodes.en: Seven hundred? That's too little! Let's say 850.

turn.prompt: Meet him halfway: offer 800, and say you'll take it. Or accept 850.

replies.en: Make it 800 and I'll take it.

replies.why: *Alıyorsunuz* says **he** is buying. You're the buyer: *alıyorum*.

nodes.tr: Durun, durun! Gitmeyin! Sekiz yüz olsun, sadece sizin için.
nodes.en: Wait, wait! Don't go! Let's say 800, just for you.
nodes.note: Walking away is the strongest move in a bargain, and every shopkeeper knows it.

turn.prompt: Accept the offer, or leave anyway.

replies.en: No, thank you. Have a good day!

nodes.tr: Harika! Hayırlı olsun! Kartla mı ödüyorsunuz, nakit mi?
nodes.en: Wonderful! Congratulations! Are you paying by card or in cash?

nodes.tr: Bin beş yüz mü? Tabii, tabii! Kartla mı ödüyorsunuz, nakit mi?
nodes.en: 1,500? Of course, of course! Are you paying by card or in cash?

nodes.note: *Güle güle kullanın*, “use it with smiles”, is said to anyone who has just bought something.

replies.en: Thank you, have a good day!
Thank you, all the best with your business!
Thanks, all the best with your business!

nodes.tr: Anlaştık! Hayırlı olsun, güle güle kullanın!
nodes.en: It's a deal! Congratulations, enjoy it!
nodes.note: *Güle güle kullanın*, “use it with smiles”, is said to anyone who has just bought something.
nodes.end: You bargained the plate down from 1,200 to 800 lira.
You paid 850 lira: a fair price, after a little bargaining.
You bought the plate, but paid more than you had to: in the bazaar the first price is only where bargaining starts.

nodes.en: All right, as you like. Come again!
nodes.end: You left without buying: there are thousands of other shops in the bazaar.

phrases.en: Will you give me a discount?
All the best with your business!
phrases.note: A goodbye for shopkeepers and anyone at work.
Said to someone who has just bought something.
